title: 246. Functions, Graphs & Transformations: Determining Domain from a Graph
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.concept: Domain of a Finite Graph Segment
questions.learningObjective: Determine the domain of a graph given as a closed line segment.
questions.question: A graph is a line segment from \((-3,2)\) to \((4,5)\) with closed dots at both endpoints. What is the domain of this graph?
questions.explanation: The domain is the set of all \(x\)-values for which the graph has a point. The segment begins at \(x=-3\) and ends at \(x=4\). Because both endpoints are closed dots, both values are included. Therefore the domain is \([-3,4]\), so option A is correct.
questions.hint: Use the leftmost and rightmost \(x\)-values of the graph, and check whether the endpoints are included.

questions.concept: Domain of a Ray with an Open Endpoint
questions.learningObjective: Determine the domain of a ray whose endpoint is excluded.
questions.question: A graph is a ray that starts at \((2,-1)\) with an open dot and extends to the right without bound. What is the domain?
questions.explanation: The ray includes all \(x\)-values greater than \(2\), but the open dot at \(x=2\) means \(x=2\) is not included. Therefore the domain is \((2,\infty)\), so option B is correct.
questions.hint: Decide whether the starting point of the ray belongs to the graph.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the domain when a graph consists of two separate rays.
questions.question: A graph consists of two rays: one ray ends at \((-1,2)\) with a closed dot and extends left without bound, and the other ray starts at \((1,3)\) with a closed dot and extends right without bound. What is the domain?
questions.explanation: The left ray includes all \(x\)-values less than or equal to \(-1\), and the right ray includes all \(x\)-values greater than or equal to \(1\). The closed dots include \(-1\) and \(1\). Therefore the domain is \((-\infty,-1]\cup[1,\infty)\), so option A is correct.
questions.hint: Find the \(x\)-values covered by each ray, and check whether each endpoint is included.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the domain of a graph that extends indefinitely left and right.
questions.question: A graph is a parabola opening upward with vertex \((0,-2)\). The arms extend indefinitely to the left and right. What is the domain?
questions.explanation: The graph exists for every real \(x\)-value because the parabola extends indefinitely in both horizontal directions. The vertex and the direction of opening affect the range, not the domain. Therefore the domain is all real numbers, so option A is correct.
questions.hint: Check whether the graph has any missing \(x\)-values along the horizontal axis.

questions.concept: Domain of a Square Root Graph
questions.learningObjective: Determine the domain of a square root curve from its starting point.
questions.question: A graph is the curve \(y=\sqrt{x+3}\), starting at \((-3,0)\) with a closed dot and extending to the right. What is the domain?
questions.explanation: The graph begins at \(x=-3\) and continues to the right without bound. Because the starting point is a closed dot, \(x=-3\) is included. Therefore the domain is \([-3,\infty)\), so option B is correct.
questions.hint: Find the leftmost \(x\)-value of the graph and check whether that point is included.

questions.concept: Domain of a Rational Graph with a Vertical Asymptote
questions.learningObjective: Determine the domain of a graph that has a vertical asymptote.
questions.question: A graph is the curve \(y=\frac{1}{x-2}\). It has a vertical asymptote at \(x=2\) and branches on both sides. What is the domain?
questions.explanation: The graph has a vertical asymptote at \(x=2\), meaning there is no point on the graph with \(x=2\). All other real \(x\)-values are used. Therefore the domain is all real numbers except \(x=2\), so option B is correct.
questions.hint: Ask whether the graph has a point with the \(x\)-value of the vertical asymptote.

questions.concept: Domain of a Graph with a Hole
questions.learningObjective: Determine the domain of a graph that has a missing point.
questions.question: A graph is a non-vertical straight line with a hole at \((1,3)\). The line extends indefinitely in both directions. What is the domain?
questions.explanation: The graph is missing the point with \(x=1\), because there is a hole at \((1,3)\). Every other real \(x\)-value has a corresponding point on the line. Therefore the domain is all real numbers except \(x=1\), so option B is correct.
questions.hint: Check whether every \(x\)-value still has a point on the graph once the hole is removed.

questions.concept: Domain of a Piecewise Graph with Disconnected Intervals
questions.learningObjective: Determine the domain of a graph formed by two disjoint segments.
questions.question: A graph consists of a segment from \((-5,1)\) with a closed dot to \((-2,3)\) with an open dot, and another segment from \((2,-1)\) with a closed dot to \((5,4)\) with a closed dot. What is the domain?
questions.explanation: The first segment includes \(x=-5\) but excludes \(x=-2\) because the endpoint at \(-2\) is open. The second segment includes \(x=2\) and \(x=5\) because both endpoints are closed. Therefore the domain is \([-5,-2)\cup[2,5]\), so option B is correct.
questions.hint: Check each endpoint separately and decide whether it is included.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the domain of an upper semicircle from its endpoints.
questions.question: A graph is the upper semicircle \(y=\sqrt{4-x^2}\), with closed dots at \((-2,0)\) and \((2,0)\). What is the domain?
questions.explanation: The semicircle exists from \(x=-2\) to \(x=2\). Because the endpoints at \(-2\) and \(2\) are closed dots, both values are included. Therefore the domain is \([-2,2]\), so option B is correct.
questions.hint: The domain is the horizontal span of the graph; check whether its endpoints are included.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the domain of a graph that consists of one isolated point.
questions.question: A graph consists of only the single point \((3,-1)\). What is the domain?
questions.explanation: The graph has a point only when \(x=3\). There are no points for any other \(x\)-value. Therefore the domain contains only the single value \(3\), so the domain is \(\{3\}\), and option A is correct.
questions.hint: List every \(x\)-value for which the graph actually has a point.
